implementation_notes: C has no interface syntax, so all five rules must be expressed through headers and opaque structs. SRP becomes one .h per reason to change; DIP becomes a struct of function pointers or an ops table passed into the consumer; ISP becomes several small headers rather than one god-header; LSP is enforced only by discipline since nothing checks it; OCP means adding a new ops table, never editing the old one.
idiom_name: opaque struct + ops table + narrow headers
pitfalls: Header cycles are the C expression of DIP violation; `#include` the contract header, never the implementation header.
Public struct definitions in headers silently expose implementation detail and destroy information hiding.
No compile-time LSP check — a mismatched ops table compiles and crashes at runtime.
